column6: Bullet 1 correction said vertex count "depends on where edges meet" then cited the cone's 1 vertex, which is not where edges meet; reworded to corners or points.
Bullet 3 ("undoing addition means subtracting the total") is a strawman; deleted, 2 bullets remain.
Bullet 3 ("water that fills the other to the brim means the second holds more") is a strawman; replaced with the real conservation misconception (pouring into a taller glass makes more water).
Q3 stem garbled ("write down most your tally marks ... through most fourth mark"); restored to "all" / "every fourth mark".
4 blocks + 2 blocks example said "The total is always 8"; corrected to 6.
Q3 stem garbled ("you primarily need to memorize half"); changed to "only need".
Q3 stem "generally means the object is longer" made the false key arguable; changed to "always".
Said > "points left" and < "points right" toward the bigger number; the point faces the smaller number. Changed to "opens to the left/right".
Q3 stem "generally has more sides" made the false key arguable (changed to "always"); Q2 explanation said any rectangle can be split into two squares (only a 2-by-1 rectangle can), removed.
Q3 stem "usually produces the same pieces" garbled; changed to "always".
Q2 stem "There is mainly one correct way" garbled; changed to "only one".
Rule "say 'half an hour' when the long hand reaches 6" would also fire at 2:30 and 3:30 and double-count on the 2:00-4:30 example; reworded to whole turns then a last half turn.
Bullet 1 belief "equal if there are the same number of groups" was incoherent; replaced with "equal if they are in the same kind of container".
Q1 stem garbled ("objects in most of the groups"); changed to "all of the groups".
Bullet 2 belief "equal parts must have the same shape" was not answered by its correction (each cut gives same-shape halves); belief reworded to "halves of a rectangle must always be rectangles".
Bullet 3 ("big numbers are too big to be even") is a strawman; replaced with judging parity by the first digit (30 is odd).
Try 7 + ? = 12 with the same card but the card holds 3, 4, 7; changed to 3 + ? = 7.
Q2 stem garbled ("mostly different kinds of shapes"; explanation quotes "completely different"); changed to "completely".

Q3 stem garbled ("looks like a rectangle at first glance is expected to have"); changed to "A rectangle must have four sides of equal length." Q4 answer called naming a tilted rectangle a "parallelogram" a mistake, but every rectangle is a parallelogram; example changed to a tilted square called a "diamond".
